title: Why Plane Windows Are Round (3 Jets Fell Apart First)
description: Every plane window you've ever looked through is round, and that's not a style choice. In the early 1950s the world's first jet airliner, the de Havilland Comet, broke up in the air three times in less than a year. The cause was hiding in the corners: a pressurised cabin swelling and relaxing on every flight, metal fatigue, and stress piling up at square-cornered openings. Here's the whole story, built in low-poly 3D: the metal balloon, the paper-clip physics, the giant water tank at Farnborough, and the fix that's on every airliner today.
